Ye jhāyino tā pajahanti sabbā, ātāpino brahmacariyaṃ carantāti ye ārammaṇūpanijjhānena lakkhaṇūpanijjhānena jhāyino vipassanaṃ ussukkāpetvā catubbidhasammappadhānapāripūriyā ātāpino maggabrahmacariyaṃ carantā adhigacchantā saddhānusārīādippabhedā paṭhamamaggaṭṭhā puggalā, tā sabbā kaṅkhā pajahanti samucchindanti maggakkhaṇe. Tato paraṃ pana tā pahīnā nāma honti, tasmā ito aññaṃ tāsaṃ accantappahānaṃ nāma natthīti adhippāyo.

Herein, 'whatever doubt, whether here or elsewhere': 'here' means doubt arising in this present existence, such as, 'Am I or am I not?'; 'elsewhere' means doubt arising concerning past or future existences, such as, 'Did I exist in the past?'. 'Whether concerning one's own experience or another's': 'one's own experience' refers to that same doubt, as described above, when it arises with one's own existence as its object; 'another's experience' refers to when it arises concerning another's existence, such as, 'Is he the Buddha or not?', or concerning another's supreme attainment. This covers whatever doubt or uncertainty exists. 'Those who meditate abandon all such doubts, ardently practicing the holy life': Those who meditate by focusing on the object or the characteristics, having made an effort in insight and, through the complete fulfillment of the fourfold right effort, are ardent; practicing and attaining the holy life of the path—these are individuals of the faith-follower type and so on, who are established in the first path. They abandon and uproot all those doubts at the moment of the path. Beyond that, those doubts are said to be abandoned. Therefore, the meaning is that there is no other complete abandonment of them beyond this.

Iti [P 0.0316] bhagavā jhānamukhena āyasmato kaṅkhārevatassa jhānasīsena ariyamaggādhigamaṃ thomento thomanāvasena udānaṃ udānesi. Teneva ca naṃ “etadaggaṃ, bhikkhave, mama sāvakānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ jhāyīnaṃ yadidaṃ kaṅkhārevato”ti (a. ni. 1.204) jhāyībhāvena etadagge ṭhapesīti.

Thus the Blessed One, praising the Venerable Kaṅkhārevata's attainment of the noble path with jhāna as its foundation, uttered this inspired utterance by way of praise. And for that very reason, he established him as foremost among his bhikkhu disciples who are meditators, saying: 'Bhikkhus, the foremost among my bhikkhu disciples who are meditators is this one, namely, Kaṅkhārevata' (AN 1.204).

Sattamasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the Seventh Sutta is finished.

8. Saṅghabhedasuttavaṇṇanā

8. Commentary on the Sutta on Schism in the Sangha

48. Aṭṭhame [V 0.0258] āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ etadavocāti abhimāre payojetvā nāḷāgiriṃ vissajjāpetvā silaṃ pavaṭṭetvā bhagavato anatthaṃ kātuṃ asakkonto “saṅghaṃ bhinditvā cakkabhedaṃ karissāmī”ti adhippāyena etaṃ “ajjatagge”tiādivacanaṃ avoca. Aññatreva bhagavatāti vinā eva bhagavantaṃ, satthāraṃ akatvāti attho. Aññatra bhikkhusaṅghāti vinā eva bhikkhusaṅghaṃ. Uposathaṃ karissāmi saṅghakammāni cāti bhagavato ovādakārakaṃ bhikkhusaṅghaṃ visuṃ katvā maṃ anuvattantehi bhikkhūhi saddhiṃ āveṇikaṃ uposathaṃ saṅghakammāni ca karissāmīti attho. Devadatto saṅghaṃ bhindissatīti bhedakarānaṃ sabbesaṃ devadattena sajjitattā ekaṃseneva devadatto ajja [M 0.0288] saṅghaṃ bhindissati dvidhā karissati. “Adhammaṃ dhammo”tiādīsu hi aṭṭhārasasu bhedakaravatthūsu yaṃkiñci ekampi vatthuṃ dīpetvā tena tena kāraṇena “imaṃ gaṇhatha, imaṃ rocethā”ti saññāpetvā salākaṃ gāhetvā visuṃ saṅghakamme kate saṅgho bhinno hoti. Vuttañhetaṃ –

48. In the eighth sutta, regarding the words 'he said this to the Venerable Ānanda': Having employed assassins, having had the elephant Nāḷāgiri unleashed, and having rolled down a rock, but being unable to harm the Blessed One, with the intention, “I will split the Sangha and cause a schism,” he spoke those words beginning with “From today onwards.” 'Apart from the Blessed One' means without the Blessed One; the meaning is, without making him the Teacher. 'Apart from the community of bhikkhus' means without the community of bhikkhus. 'I will perform the Uposatha and the formal acts of the Sangha' means: “Having separated from the community of bhikkhus that follows the instructions of the Blessed One, I will perform a separate Uposatha and separate formal acts of the Sangha together with the bhikkhus who follow me.” 'Devadatta will split the Sangha': since all the schismatics have been prepared by Devadatta, it is certain that today Devadatta will split the Sangha, that he will divide it in two. For in regard to the eighteen grounds for causing schism, such as “non-Dhamma is Dhamma,” when, by expounding even a single ground, and for that reason making them agree by saying, “Accept this, approve of this,” and having them take a voting ticket, a separate formal act of the Sangha is performed, the Sangha becomes split. For it has been said:

“Pañcahi, upāli, ākārehi saṅgho bhijjati kammena uddesena voharanto anussāvanena salākaggāhenā”ti (pari. 458).

“Upāli, the Sangha is split in five ways: by a formal act, by a recitation, by declaring, by an announcement, and by the taking of voting tickets” (Pari 458).

Tattha kammenāti apalokanakammādīsu catūsu kammesu aññatarena kammena. Uddesenāti [P 0.0317] pañcasu pātimokkhuddesesu aññatarena uddesena. Voharantoti tāhi tāhi uppattīhi “adhammaṃ dhammo”tiādīni (a. ni. 10.37; cūḷava. 352) aṭṭhārasabhedakaravatthūni dīpento. Anussāvanenāti “nanu tumhe jānātha mayhaṃ uccākulā pabbajitabhāvaṃ bahussutabhāvañca, mādiso nāma uddhammaṃ ubbinayaṃ gāheyyāti kiṃ tumhākaṃ cittampi uppādetuṃ yuttaṃ, kimahaṃ apāyato na bhāyāmī”tiādinā nayena kaṇṇamūle vacībhedaṃ katvā anussāvanena. Salākaggāhenāti evaṃ anussāvetvā tesaṃ cittaṃ upatthambhetvā anāvattidhamme katvā “gaṇhatha imaṃ salāka”nti salākaggāhena.

Herein, 'by a formal act' means by any one of the four formal acts, beginning with the act of seeking consent. 'By recitation' means by any one of the five recitations of the Pātimokkha. 'By declaring' means expounding the eighteen grounds for causing schism with those various points, such as “non-Dhamma is Dhamma” (AN 10.37; Cv.VII.5.1). 'By an announcement' means by an announcement made by whispering in the ear in this way: “Surely you know that I have gone forth from a high family and am very learned. Is it proper for you even to entertain the thought that one such as I would take up what is not the Dhamma and not the Vinaya? Do I not fear the plane of misery?” 'By the taking of voting tickets' means, having thus made the announcement, having bolstered their minds and made them irreversible, by the taking of voting tickets, saying, “Take this voting ticket.”

Ettha ca kammameva uddeso vā pamāṇaṃ, vohārānussāvanasalākaggāhā pana pubbabhāgā. Aṭṭhārasavatthudīpanavasena hi voharantena tattha rucijananatthaṃ anussāvetvā salākāya gāhitāyapi abhinnova hoti saṅgho. Yadā panevaṃ cattāro vā atirekā vā salākaṃ gāhetvā āveṇikaṃ uddesaṃ vā kammaṃ vā karonti, tadā saṅgho bhinno nāma hoti. Devadatto ca sabbaṃ saṅghabhedassa pubbabhāgaṃ [V 0.0259] nipphādetvā “ekaṃseneva ajja āveṇikaṃ uposathaṃ saṅghakammañca karissāmī”ti cintetvā “ajjatagge”tiādivacanaṃ avoca. Tenāha – “ajja, bhante, devadatto saṅghaṃ bhindissatī”ti. Yato avocumhā “bhedakarānaṃ sabbesaṃ devadattena sajjitattā”ti.

Here, the formal act or the recitation is the decisive factor; the declaring, announcing, and taking of voting tickets, however, are preliminary stages. For when one declares by way of expounding the eighteen grounds, and after announcing in order to generate approval for them, even when the voting tickets have been taken, the Sangha is still undivided. But when four or more, having taken the voting tickets in this way, perform a separate recitation or formal act, then the Sangha is said to be split. And Devadatta, having completed all the preliminary stages for schism in the Sangha, thinking, “It is certain that today I will perform a separate Uposatha and a separate formal act of the Sangha,” spoke the words beginning, “From today onwards….” That is why it was said: “Today, venerable sir, Devadatta will split the Sangha.” And this is why we said: “since all the schismatics have been prepared by Devadatta.”

Etamatthaṃ viditvāti etaṃ avīcimahānirayuppattisaṃvattaniyaṃ kappaṭṭhiyaṃ atekicchaṃ devadattena nibbattiyamānaṃ saṅghabhedakammaṃ sabbākārato viditvā[M 0.0289]. Imaṃ udānanti kusalākusalesu yathākkamaṃ sappurisāsappurisasabhāgavisabhāgapaṭipattivasena pana sukusalāti idamatthavibhāvanaṃ imaṃ udānaṃ udānesi.

'Having understood this matter' means: having understood in all its aspects this act of schism in the Sangha being brought about by Devadatta, which leads to arising in the Avīci great hell, lasts for an aeon, and is incurable. 'This inspired utterance': he uttered this inspired utterance, which is an explanation of this meaning concerning what is wholesome and unwholesome, namely, the similar and dissimilar conduct of true men and untrue men, and what is very wholesome.

Tattha sukaraṃ sādhunā sādhūti attano paresañca hitaṃ sādhetīti [P 0.0318] sādhu, sammāpaṭipanno. Tena sādhunā sāriputtādinā sāvakena paccekabuddhena sammāsambuddhena aññena vā lokiyasādhunā sādhu sundaraṃ bhaddakaṃ attano paresañca hitasukhāvahaṃ sukaraṃ sukhena kātuṃ sakkā. Sādhu pāpena dukkaranti tadeva pana vuttalakkhaṇaṃ sādhu pāpena devadattādinā pāpapuggalena dukkaraṃ kātuṃ na sakkā, na so taṃ kātuṃ sakkotīti attho. Pāpaṃ pāpena sukaranti pāpaṃ asundaraṃ attano paresañca anatthāvahaṃ pāpena yathāvuttapāpapuggalena sukaraṃ sukhena kātuṃ sakkuṇeyya. Pāpamariyehi dukkaranti ariyehi pana buddhādīhi taṃ taṃ pāpaṃ dukkaraṃ durabhisambhavaṃ. Setughātoyeva hi tesanti satthā dīpeti.

Herein, 'good is easy for the good': one who accomplishes their own and others’ welfare is a good person (sādhu), one of right practice. By that good person—a disciple such as Sāriputta, a paccekabuddha, a perfectly enlightened one, or another worldly good person—what is good, beautiful, auspicious, and brings welfare and happiness to oneself and others, is easy to do (sukaraṃ); it can be done with ease. 'Good is hard for the bad': that same good with the characteristics described is hard to do (dukkaraṃ) for a bad person such as Devadatta; the meaning is that they are unable to do it. 'Evil is easy for the bad': what is evil, ugly, and brings harm to oneself and others is easy to do (sukaraṃ) for a bad person as described; they can do it with ease. 'Evil is hard for the noble': but for the noble ones, such as the Buddhas, that evil is hard to do (dukkaraṃ), difficult to accomplish. The Teacher shows that for them this would be the very destruction of the bridge.

Aṭṭhamasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the Eighth Sutta is finished.

9. Sadhāyamānasuttavaṇṇanā

9. Commentary on the Sadhāyamāna Sutta

49. Navame māṇavakāti taruṇā. Paṭhame yobbane ṭhitā brāhmaṇakumārakā idhādhippetā.

49. In the ninth sutta, 'young men' means youths. Herein, young brahmin boys established in the prime of youth are intended.

Sadhāyamānarūpāti uppaṇḍanajātikaṃ vacanaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ. Aññesaṃ uppaṇḍentā sadhanti, tadatthavacanasīlāti attho. Tassāyaṃ vacanattho – sadhanaṃ sadho, taṃ ācikkhantīti sadhayamānāti vattabbe dīghaṃ katvā “sadhāyamānā”ti vuttaṃ. Atha vā visesato sasedhe viya attānaṃ āvadantīti sadhāyamānā. Te evaṃ sabhāvatāya “sadhāyamānarūpā”ti vuttaṃ. “Saddāyamānarūpā”tipi [V 0.0260] pāṭho, uccāsaddamahāsaddaṃ karontāti attho. Bhagavato avidūre atikkamantīti bhagavato savanavisaye taṃ taṃ mukhāruḷhaṃ vadantā atiyanti.

`Of a boastful nature` is said with reference to speech of a boastful kind. They boast over others, being inclined to speak for that purpose; this is the meaning. The meaning of this word is as follows: `sadhana` is `sadha` (boasting); because they declare it, it should be said `sadhayamānā`, but by making the vowel long, `sadhāyamānā` is said. Or alternatively, they are `sadhāyamānā` because they speak of themselves excessively, as if binding themselves with special qualities. Because of such a nature, they are called `of a boastful nature`. There is also the reading `saddāyamānarūpā`, meaning they make a loud noise, a great noise. `Passing not far from the Blessed One` means they go by speaking whatever comes to their mouths within the Blessed One's range of hearing.

Etamatthaṃ [M 0.0290] viditvāti etaṃ tesaṃ vācāya asaññatabhāvaṃ [P 0.0319] jānitvā tadatthadīpakaṃ dhammasaṃvegavasena imaṃ udānaṃ udānesi.

`Having understood this matter` means: having known their lack of restraint in speech, he uttered this inspired utterance to illuminate that matter by way of spiritual urgency.

Tattha parimuṭṭhāti dandhā muṭṭhassatino. Paṇḍitābhāsāti paṇḍitapatirūpakā “ke aññe jānanti, mayamevettha jānāmā”ti tasmiṃ tasmiṃ atthe attānameva jānantaṃ katvā samudācaraṇato. Vācāgocarabhāṇinoti yesaṃ vācā eva gocaro visayo, te vācāgocarabhāṇino, vācāvatthumattasseva bhāṇino atthassa apariññātattā. Atha vā vācāya agocaraṃ ariyānaṃ kathāya avisayaṃ musāvādaṃ bhaṇantīti vācāgocarabhāṇino. Atha vā “gocarabhāṇino”ti ettha ākārassa rassabhāvo kato. Vācāgocarā, na satipaṭṭhānādigocarā bhāṇinova. Kathaṃ bhāṇino? Yāvicchanti mukhāyāmaṃ attano yāva mukhāyāmaṃ yāva mukhappasāraṇaṃ icchanti, tāva pasāretvā bhāṇino, paresu gāravena, attano avisayatāya ca mukhasaṅkocaṃ na karontīti attho. Atha vā vācāgocarā eva hutvā bhāṇino, sayaṃ ajānitvā parapattikā eva hutvā vattāroti attho. Tato eva yāvicchanti mukhāyāmaṃ yena vacanena sāvetabbā, taṃ acintetvā yāvadeva attano mukhappasāraṇamattaṃ icchantīti attho. Yena nītā na taṃ vidūti yena muṭṭhassaccādinā nillajjabhāvaṃ paṇḍitamānībhāvañca nītā “mayamevaṃ bhaṇāmā”ti, taṃ tathā attano bhaṇantassa kāraṇaṃ na vidū, aviddasuno asūrā na jānantīti attho.

Herein, `heedless` means sluggish, of confused mindfulness. `Pretenders to wisdom` means those who resemble the wise, because they conduct themselves making themselves out to be the only ones who know in this or that matter, thinking: ‘Who else knows? We alone know here!’ `Speakers whose pasture is speech` means those for whom speech alone is their pasture, their domain; they are speakers of the mere letter of the speech because the meaning is not fully understood. Or alternatively, they are `speakers whose pasture is speech` because they speak falsehood, which is not the pasture of speech, not the domain of the talk of the noble ones. Or alternatively, in `gocarabhāṇino` the `ā` has been shortened. They are speakers whose pasture is speech, not those whose pasture is the foundations of mindfulness and so on. How are they speakers? `Whatever opening of the mouth they wish for`: they are speakers who extend their mouths as much as they wish to open them, meaning they do not restrain their mouths out of respect for others or because of their own lack of knowledge. Or alternatively, being speakers whose pasture is speech, they are speakers who speak without knowing for themselves, being mere repeaters of others' beliefs. Therefore, `whatever opening of the mouth they wish for` means that without considering by what words they should make themselves heard, they desire only the mere opening of their own mouths. `By what they are led, that they do not know` means: they do not know that reason for their speaking in such a way—namely, that by which they are led to shamelessness and the conceit of being wise through confused mindfulness and so on, thinking, ‘We speak thus.’ Being ignorant, not being true men, they do not know; this is the meaning.

Navamasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the ninth sutta is finished.

10. Cūḷapanthakasuttavaṇṇanā

10. Commentary on the Cūḷapanthaka Sutta

50. Dasame cūḷapanthakoti mahāpanthakattherassa kaniṭṭhabhātikattā panthe jātattā ca daharakāle laddhavohārena aparabhāgepi ayamāyasmā “cūḷapanthako”tveva paññāyittha. Guṇavisesehi pana chaḷabhiñño pabhinnapaṭisambhido “etadaggaṃ, bhikkhave, mama sāvakānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ [M 0.0291][V 0.0261] manomayaṃ kāyaṃ abhinimminantānaṃ yadidaṃ cūḷapanthako, cetovivaṭṭakusalānaṃ [P 0.0320] yadidaṃ cūḷapanthako”ti dvīsu (a. ni. 1.199) ṭhānesu bhagavatā etadagge ṭhapito asītiyā mahāsāvakesu abbhantaro.

50. In the tenth sutta: Because he was the younger brother of the Elder Mahāpanthaka and was born on the road, this venerable one was known by the designation `Cūḷapanthaka` acquired in his youth, and he continued to be known as `Cūḷapanthaka` even in later times. But on account of his special qualities—possessing the six supernormal knowledges and having attained the analytical knowledges—he was placed at the top by the Blessed One in two instances: ‘Bhikkhus, foremost among my bhikkhu disciples who create a mind-made body is Cūḷapanthaka; and foremost among those skilled in the unfolding of mind is Cūḷapanthaka’ (AN 1.24). He is included among the eighty great disciples.

So ekadivasaṃ pacchābhattaṃ piṇḍapātappaṭikkanto attano divāṭṭhāne divāvihāraṃ nisinno samāpattīhi divasabhāgaṃ vītināmetvā sāyanhasamayaṃ upāsakesu dhammassavanatthaṃ anāgatesu eva vihāramajjhaṃ pavisitvā bhagavati gandhakuṭiyaṃ nisinne “akālo tāva bhagavato upaṭṭhānaṃ upasaṅkamitu”nti gandhakuṭipamukhe ekamantaṃ nisīdi pallaṅkaṃ ābhujitvā. Tena vuttaṃ – “tena kho pana samayena āyasmā cūḷapanthako bhagavato avidūre nisinno hoti pallaṅkaṃ ābhujitvā ujuṃ kāyaṃ paṇidhāya parimukhaṃ satiṃ upaṭṭhapetvā”ti. So hi tadā kālaparicchedaṃ katvā samāpattiṃ samāpajjitvā nisīdi.

One day, having returned from the alms round after the meal, he sat down for his day's abiding in his daytime quarters and spent the day in meditative attainments. In the evening, before the lay followers had arrived to hear the Dhamma, he entered the middle of the monastery. Seeing the Blessed One seated in the fragrant chamber, he thought, ‘It is not yet the time to approach and attend on the Blessed One,’ and sat down to one side at the entrance to the fragrant chamber, having folded his legs crosswise. Hence it was said: ‘Now at that time, the Venerable Cūḷapanthaka was sitting not far from the Blessed One, having folded his legs crosswise, set his body erect, and established mindfulness before him.’ For at that time he sat having entered an attainment after making a determination of time.

Etamatthaṃ viditvāti etaṃ āyasmato cūḷapanthakassa kāyacittānaṃ sammāpaṇihitabhāvasaṅkhātaṃ atthaṃ jānitvā. Imaṃ udānanti aññopi yo passaddhakāyo sabbiriyāpathesu upaṭṭhitassati samāhito, tassa bhikkhuno anupādā parinibbānapariyosānassa visesādhigamassa tattha pātubhāvavibhāvanaṃ imaṃ udānaṃ udānesi.

`Having understood this matter` means: having known this matter, that is, the well-established state of the Venerable Cūḷapanthaka's body and mind, he uttered this inspired utterance. This inspired utterance clarifies the manifestation of the attainment of distinction that culminates in final Nibbāna without clinging for any other bhikkhu, too, whose body is tranquil, whose mindfulness is established in all postures, and who is concentrated.

Tattha ṭhitena kāyenāti kāyadvārikassa asaṃvarassa pahānena akaraṇena sammā ṭhapitena copanakāyena, tathā cakkhādīnaṃ indriyānaṃ nibbisevanabhāvakaraṇena suṭṭhu ṭhapitena pañcadvārikakāyena, saṃyatahatthapādatāya hatthakukkuccādīnaṃ abhāvato apariphandanena ṭhitena karajakāyena cāti saṅkhepato sabbenapi kāyena nibbikāratāsaṅkhātena niccalabhāvena ṭhitena. Etenassa sīlapārisuddhi dassitā. Itthambhūtalakkhaṇe ca idaṃ karaṇavacanaṃ. Ṭhitena cetasāti cittassa ṭhitiparidīpanena samādhisampadaṃ dasseti. Samādhi hi cittassa ‘ṭhitī’ti vuccati. Tasmā samathavasena vipassanāvaseneva vā ekaggatāya sati cittaṃ ārammaṇe ekodibhāvūpagamanena ṭhitaṃ nāma hoti, na aññathā. Idañca yathāvuttakāyacittānaṃ ṭhapanaṃ samādahanaṃ sabbasmiṃ kāle sabbesu ca iriyāpathesu icchitabbanti dassento āha – “tiṭṭhaṃ nisinno uda vā sayāno”ti[M 0.0292]. Tattha [P 0.0321] vā-saddo aniyamattho. Tena tiṭṭhanto vā nisinno vā sayāno vā tadaññiriyāpatho vāti ayamattho dīpito hotīti caṅkamanassāpi idha saṅgaho veditabbo.

`With body established` means: with the active body well-established through the abandoning and non-commission of lack of restraint at the body door; similarly, with the body at the five doors well-established by not indulging the faculties of the eye, etc.; and with the physical body established by not trembling, due to the absence of fidgeting with the hands, etc., because the hands and feet are restrained. In brief, it means established with the entire body in a state of immobility designated as being without modification. By this, his purity of virtue is shown. And this instrumental case indicates the state of being so. `With mind established`: by indicating the stability of the mind, this shows the accomplishment of concentration. For concentration is called the ‘stability’ of the mind. Therefore, when there is one-pointedness by way of either serenity or insight, the mind is said to be established by having reached a unified state on its object, not otherwise. And showing that this establishing and composing of body and mind as described is desirable at all times and in all postures, he said: `Whether standing, sitting, or lying down.` Herein, the word `vā` (or) has the meaning of non-restriction. By this, the meaning ‘whether standing or sitting or lying down or in another posture’ is clarified, so walking should also be understood as included here.

Etaṃ [V 0.0262] satiṃ bhikkhu adhiṭṭhahānoti yāya pageva parisuddhasamācāro kāyacittaduṭṭhullabhāvūpasamanena kāyaṃ cittañca asāraddhaṃ katvā paṭiladdhāya anavajjasukhādhiṭṭhāya kāyacittapassaddhivasena cittaṃ lahuṃ muduṃ kammaññañca katvā sammā ṭhapento samādahanto kammaṭṭhānaṃ paribrūheti matthakañca pāpeti, taṃ eva kammaṭṭhānānuyogassa ādimajjhapariyosānesu bahūpakāraṃ satiṃ bhikkhu adhiṭṭhahāno sīlavisodhanaṃ ādiṃ katvā yāva visesādhigamā tattha tattha adhiṭṭhahantoti attho. Labhetha pubbāpariyaṃ visesanti so evaṃ satiārakkhena cetasā kammaṭṭhānaṃ uparūpari vaḍḍhento brūhento phātiṃ karonto pubbāpariyaṃ pubbāpariyavantaṃ pubbāparabhāgena pavattaṃ uḷāruḷāratarādibhedavisesaṃ labheyya.

`A bhikkhu should resolve on this mindfulness` means: a bhikkhu should resolve on that very mindfulness which is of great help at the beginning, middle, and end of the application to the meditation subject. By means of this mindfulness—being already of pure conduct, having made body and mind unagitated by calming their coarseness, having gained the support of blameless bliss, and having made the mind light, malleable, and wieldy through the tranquility of body and mind—he properly establishes and composes it, develops the meditation subject, and brings it to a climax. The meaning is that he should resolve on it at each stage, beginning with the purification of virtue up to the attainment of distinction. `He would attain a prior and posterior distinction` means: thus, with a mind guarded by mindfulness, by developing, cultivating, and expanding the meditation subject again and again, he would attain a prior and posterior distinction—that is, a distinction possessing prior and posterior stages, proceeding by prior and posterior parts, a distinction with various gradations such as grosser and more sublime.

Tattha duvidho pubbāpariyaviseso samathavasena vipassanāvasena cāti. Tesu samathavasena tāva nimittuppattito paṭṭhāya yāva nevasaññānāsaññāyatanavasībhāvo, tāva pavatto bhāvanāviseso pubbāpariyaviseso. Vipassanāvasena pana rūpamukhena abhinivisantassa rūpadhammapariggahato, itarassa nāmadhammapariggahato paṭṭhāya yāva arahattādhigamo, tāva pavatto bhāvanāviseso pubbāpariyaviseso. Ayameva ca idhādhippeto.

Herein, the prior and posterior distinction is twofold: by way of serenity and by way of insight. Of these, by way of serenity, the distinction in development that proceeds from the arising of the sign up to mastery over the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception is the prior and posterior distinction. By way of insight, however, for one who enters by way of form, the distinction in development that proceeds from the comprehension of material phenomena, or for another, from the comprehension of mental phenomena, up to the attainment of arahantship, is the prior and posterior distinction. And it is just this latter that is intended here.

Laddhāna pubbāpariyaṃ visesanti pubbāpariyavisesaṃ ukkaṃsapāramippattaṃ arahattaṃ labhitvā. Adassanaṃ maccurājassa gaccheti jīvitupacchedavasena sabbesaṃ sattānaṃ abhibhavanato maccurājasaṅkhātassa maraṇassa visayabhūtaṃ bhavattayaṃ samatikkantattā adassanaṃ agocaraṃ gaccheyya. Imasmiṃ vagge yaṃ avuttaṃ, taṃ heṭṭhā vuttanayamevāti.

`Having attained the prior and posterior distinction` means: having attained arahantship, which is the prior and posterior distinction that has reached the peak of perfection. `He would go beyond the sight of the King of Death` means: because he has transcended the three realms of existence—which are the domain of death, called the King of Death because it overpowers all beings by cutting off their life—he would go to a state of not being seen, of being beyond its range. In this chapter, whatever has not been said should be understood in the same way as explained above.

Dasamasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the tenth sutta is finished.

Niṭṭhitā ca mahāvaggavaṇṇanā.

And the commentary on the Great Chapter is finished.

6. Jaccandhavaggo

6. The Chapter on the Blind from Birth

1. Āyusaṅkhārossajjanasuttavaṇṇanā

1. Commentary on the Discourse on Relinquishing the Life-Span

51. Jaccandhavaggassa [V 0.0263][M 0.0293][P 0.0322] paṭhame vesāliyantiādi heṭṭhā vuttatthameva. Vesāliṃ piṇḍāya pāvisīti kadā pāvisi? Ukkācelato nikkhamitvā vesāliṃ gatakāle. Bhagavā hi veḷuvagāmake vassaṃ vasitvā tato nikkhamitvā anupubbena sāvatthiṃ patvā jetavane vihāsi. Tasmiṃ kāle dhammasenāpati attano āyusaṅkhāraṃ oloketvā “sattāhameva pavattissatī”ti ñatvā bhagavantaṃ anujānāpetvā nāḷakagāmaṃ gantvā tattha mātaraṃ sotāpattiphale patiṭṭhāpetvā parinibbāyi. Satthā cundena ābhatā tassa dhātuyo gahetvā dhātucetiyaṃ kārāpetvā mahābhikkhusaṅghaparivuto rājagahaṃ agamāsi. Tattha gatakāle āyasmā mahāmoggallāno parinibbāyi. Bhagavā tassapi dhātuyo gahetvā cetiyaṃ kārāpetvā rājagahato nikkhamitvā anupubbena ukkācelaṃ agamāsi. Tattha gaṅgātīre bhikkhusaṅghaparivuto nisīditvā aggasāvakānaṃ parinibbānappaṭisaṃyuttaṃ dhammaṃ desetvā ukkācelato nikkhamitvā vesāliṃ agamāsi. Evaṃ gato bhagavā “pubbaṇhasamayaṃ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya vesāliṃ piṇḍāya pāvisī”ti vuccati. Tena vuttaṃ – “ukkācelato nikkhamitvā vesāliṃ gatakāle”ti.

51. In the first sutta of the Jaccandhavagga, the words 'in Vesāli,' etc., have the same meaning as previously explained. 'He entered Vesāli for alms-food'—when did he enter? When he went to Vesāli after departing from Ukkācelā. For the Blessed One had spent the rains residence in Veḷuvagāma, then left there and gradually reached Sāvatthi, where he dwelt in Jetavana. At that time, the General of the Dhamma, having reviewed his own life-span, knew, 'It will last for only seven more days,' and after obtaining permission from the Blessed One, he went to Nāḷakagāma. There, he established his mother in the fruit of stream-entry and then attained final Nibbāna. The Teacher had Cunda bring his relics, and after having a relic shrine built for them, he set out for Rājagaha accompanied by a great assembly of monks. While he was there, the Venerable Mahāmoggallāna attained final Nibbāna. The Blessed One also collected his relics, had a shrine built for them, and then left Rājagaha, gradually proceeding to Ukkācelā. There, seated on the bank of the Ganges surrounded by the Saṅgha of monks, he taught the Dhamma connected with the final Nibbāna of his chief disciples. Then, leaving Ukkācelā, he went to Vesāli. Thus it is said that the Blessed One, 'having dressed in the morning, took his bowl and robe and entered Vesāli for alms-food.' Therefore it is stated: 'When he went to Vesāli after departing from Ukkācelā.'

Nisīdananti idha cammakkhaṇḍaṃ adhippetaṃ. Cāpālaṃ cetiyanti pubbe cāpālassa nāma yakkhassa vasitaṭṭhānaṃ “cāpālacetiya”nti [P 0.0323] paññāyittha. Tattha bhagavato katavihāropi tāya ruḷhiyā “cāpālacetiya”nti vuccati. Udenaṃ cetiyanti evamādīsupi eseva nayo. Sattambanti kikissa kira kāsirañño dhītaro satta kumāriyo saṃvegajātā rājagehato nikkhamitvā yattha padhānaṃ padahiṃsu, taṃ ṭhānaṃ “sattambaṃ cetiya”nti vadanti. Bahuputtanti bahupāroho eko nigrodharukkho, tasmiṃ adhivatthaṃ devataṃ bahū manussā putte patthenti, tadupādāya taṃ ṭhānaṃ “bahuputtaṃ cetiya”nti paññāyittha. Sārandadanti sārandadassa nāma yakkhassa vasitaṭṭhānaṃ. Iti sabbāneva tāni buddhuppādato pubbe devatāpariggahitattā cetiyavohārena voharitāni[M 0.0294], bhagavato vihāre katepi ca tatheva paññāyanti. Ramaṇīyāti ettha vesāliyā tāva [V 0.0264] bhūmibhāgasampattiyā puggalasampattiyā sulabhapaccayatāya ca ramaṇīyabhāvo veditabbo. Vihārānaṃ pana nagarato nātidūratāya nāccāsannatāya gamanāgamanasampattiyā anākiṇṇavihāraṭṭhānatāya chāyūdakasampattiyā pavivekapatirūpatāya ca ramaṇīyatā daṭṭhabbā. Cattāro iddhipādāti ettha iddhipādapadassa attho heṭṭhā vuttoyeva. Bhāvitāti vaḍḍhitā. Bahulīkatāti punappunaṃ katā. Yānīkatāti yuttayānaṃ viya katā. Vatthukatāti patiṭṭhaṭṭhena vatthu viya katā. Anuṭṭhitāti adhiṭṭhitā. Paricitāti samantato citā suvaḍḍhitā. Susamāraddhāti suṭṭhu samāraddhā, ativiya sammā nipphāditāti.

'Sitting mat' here refers to a piece of hide. 'The Cāpāla Shrine' was formerly the dwelling place of a yakkha named Cāpāla, and so it became known as the 'Cāpāla Cetiya.' Even the monastery built there for the Blessed One is called the 'Cāpāla Cetiya' by that established usage. The same principle applies in cases such as 'the Udena Shrine.' 'The Sattamba Shrine': it is said that seven princesses, daughters of King Kikī of Kāsi, became stirred with a sense of urgency, left the royal palace, and practiced striving at a certain place; that place is called the 'Sattamba Cetiya.' 'The Bahuputta Shrine': there was a single banyan tree with many offshoots. Because many people desiring sons would pray to the deity dwelling in it, that place became known as the 'Bahuputta Cetiya.' 'The Sārandada Shrine' was the dwelling place of a yakkha named Sārandada. Thus, all these places, having been possessed by deities before the arising of the Buddha, were designated as shrines. And even after monasteries were built there for the Blessed One, they continued to be known by the same designations. Regarding 'delightful': here, the delightfulness of Vesālī should be understood in terms of its excellent terrain, the excellence of its people, and the ready availability of requisites. As for the monasteries, their delightfulness is to be seen in their being neither too far from the city nor too close, their ease of access for coming and going, their uncrowded locations, their endowment with shade and water, and their suitability for seclusion. Regarding 'the four bases for spiritual power': the meaning of the term 'bases for spiritual power' has been explained above. 'Developed' means augmented. 'Made much of' means done repeatedly. 'Made a vehicle' means made like a yoked vehicle. 'Made a foundation' means made like a basis, in the sense of being established. 'Undertaken' means resolved upon. 'Well-practiced' means accumulated all around and well-developed. 'Well-begun' means well undertaken, exceedingly well accomplished.

Evaṃ aniyamena kathetvā puna niyametvā dassetuṃ, “tathāgatassa kho”tiādimāha. Ettha ca kappanti āyukappaṃ. Tiṭṭheyyāti tasmiṃ tasmiṃ kāle yaṃ manussānaṃ āyuppamāṇaṃ, taṃ paripuṇṇaṃ katvā tiṭṭheyya dhareyya. Kappāvasesaṃ vāti “appaṃ vā bhiyyo vā”ti (dī. ni. 2.7; a. ni. 7.74) vuttaṃ vassasatato atirekaṃ vā. Mahāsīvatthero panāha – “buddhānaṃ aṭṭhāne gajjitaṃ nāma natthi. Yatheva hi veḷuvagāmake uppannaṃ māraṇantikaṃ vedanaṃ dasa māse vikkhambhesi, evaṃ punappunaṃ taṃ samāpattiṃ samāpajjitvā vikkhambhento imaṃ bhaddakappameva [P 0.0324] tiṭṭheyyā”ti. Kasmā pana na ṭhitoti? Upādinnakasarīraṃ nāma khaṇḍiccādīhi abhibhuyyati, buddhā ca pana khaṇḍiccādibhāvaṃ appatvā pañcame āyukoṭṭhāse bahujanassa piyamanāpakāleyeva parinibbāyanti. Buddhānubuddhesu aggasāvakamahāsāvakesu parinibbutesu aparivārena ekakeneva ṭhātabbaṃ hoti, daharasāmaṇeraparivārena vā. Tato “aho buddhānaṃ parisā”ti hīḷetabbataṃ āpajjeyya, tasmā na ṭhitoti. Evaṃ vuttepi so pana na ruccati, “āyukappo”ti idameva aṭṭhakathāya niyamitaṃ.

Having spoken thus without restriction, he then specifies by saying, 'For the Tathāgata…' Here, 'kappa' refers to the life-span. 'He could remain' means he could stay, sustaining the full measure of the human life-span at any given time. 'Or for the remainder of the kappa' refers to what is stated as 'for a little while or longer,' that is, for more than a hundred years. However, the Elder Mahāsīva said: 'There is no such thing as a Buddha making an empty boast. Just as he suppressed for ten months the death-threatening pain that arose in Veḷuvagāma, so too, by repeatedly entering that meditative attainment and suppressing it, he could have remained for this entire fortunate aeon.' But why did he not remain? Because the appropriated physical body is overcome by decay and the like. The Buddhas, however, not reaching a state of decay and the like, pass into final Nibbāna in the fifth segment of their life-span, precisely when it is most pleasing and agreeable to the multitude. When the chief disciples and great disciples who follow the Buddha have attained final Nibbāna, he would have to remain alone without a retinue, or with only young novices. Then people might disparage him, saying, 'Alas, the Buddha’s assembly!' Therefore, he did not remain. Even when this is said, that view is not accepted; it is just this—'the life-span'—that is specified by the commentary as the meaning of 'kappa'.

Oḷārike [M 0.0295] nimitteti thūle saññuppādane. Thūlasaññuppādanañhetaṃ, “tiṭṭhatu bhagavā kappa”nti sakalakappaṃ avaṭṭhānayācanāya yadidaṃ “yassa kassaci, ānanda, cattāro iddhipādā bhāvitā”tiādinā aññāpadesena attano caturiddhipādabhāvanānubhāvena kappaṃ avaṭṭhānasamatthatāvibhāvanaṃ. Obhāseti pākaṭavacane. Pākaṭañcetaṃ vacanaṃ pariyāyaṃ muñcitvā ujukameva attano adhippāyavibhāvanaṃ.

'The gross sign' means a coarse intimation. This coarse intimation is for the sake of eliciting the request, 'May the Blessed One remain for the aeon.' It consists of this: the declaration, by way of the indirect statement beginning, 'Ānanda, for anyone who has developed the four bases for spiritual power…,' of his own ability to remain for the aeon through the power of having developed the four bases for spiritual power. 'He makes it obvious' means in plain speech. And this is plain speech: abandoning indirect language, it is a direct explanation of his own intention.

Bahujanahitāyāti mahājanassa hitatthāya. Bahujanasukhāyāti mahājanassa sukhatthāya. Lokānukampāyāti sattalokassa anukampaṃ paṭicca. Katarassa sattalokassa? Yo bhagavato dhammadesanaṃ sutvā paṭivijjhati, amatapānaṃ pivati, tassa. Bhagavato hi dhammacakkappavattanasuttadesanāya [V 0.0265] aññātakoṇḍaññappamukhā aṭṭhārasa brahmakoṭiyo dhammaṃ paṭivijjhiṃsu. Evaṃ yāva subhaddaparibbājakavinayanā dhammapaṭividdhasattānaṃ gaṇanā natthi, mahāsamayasuttaṃ maṅgalasuttaṃ cūḷarāhulovādasuttaṃ samacittasuttanti imesaṃ catunnaṃ suttānaṃ desanākāle abhisamayappattasattānaṃ paricchedo natthi, etassa aparimāṇassa sattalokassa anukampāya bhagavato ṭhānaṃ jātaṃ. Evaṃ anāgatepi bhavissatīti adhippāyena vadati. Devamanussānanti na kevalaṃ devamanussānaṃyeva, avasesānaṃ nāgasupaṇṇādīnampi atthāya hitāya sukhāya bhagavato ṭhānaṃ hoti. Sahetukapaṭisandhike pana maggaphalasacchikiriyāya bhabbapuggale dassetuṃ evaṃ vuttaṃ, tasmā aññesampi atthatthāya hitatthāya sukhatthāya bhagavā tiṭṭhatūti attho. Tattha atthāyāti idhalokasampattiatthāya[P 0.0325]. Hitāyāti paralokasampattihetubhūtahitatthāya. Sukhāyāti nibbānadhātusukhatthāya. Purimaṃ pana hitasukhaggahaṇaṃ sabbasādhāraṇavasena veditabbaṃ.

'For the welfare of the many' means for the benefit of the multitude. 'For the happiness of the many' means for the happiness of the multitude. 'Out of compassion for the world' means on account of compassion for the world of beings. For which world of beings? For those who, upon hearing the Blessed One’s teaching, penetrate it and drink the deathless. Indeed, at the time of the Blessed One’s teaching of the Dhammacakkappavattana Sutta, eighteen crores of brahmas, led by Aññāta Koṇḍañña, penetrated the Dhamma. Thus, up to the taming of the wanderer Subhadda, there is no counting the beings who have penetrated the Dhamma. At the time of the teaching of the Mahāsamaya Sutta, the Maṅgala Sutta, the Cūḷarāhulovāda Sutta, and the Samacitta Sutta, there is no limit to the beings who attained the breakthrough. It is out of compassion for this immeasurable world of beings that the Blessed One should remain. He speaks with the intention that this will be so in the future as well. 'For devas and humans': the Blessed One’s remaining is not only for the good, welfare, and happiness of devas and humans, but also for the remaining beings such as nāgas and supaṇṇas. However, this was said in order to indicate those capable persons with a rooted rebirth-linking who are fit to realize the path and its fruits. Therefore, the meaning is: 'May the Blessed One remain for the good, welfare, and happiness of others too.' Here, 'for the good' (atthāya) means for the sake of prosperity in this world. 'For the welfare' (hitāya) means for the sake of the welfare that is the cause of prosperity in the next world. 'For the happiness' (sukhāya) means for the sake of the happiness of the Nibbāna element. The earlier mention of 'welfare' and 'happiness' should be understood in a general sense.

Yathā taṃ mārena pariyuṭṭhitacittoti ettha nti nipātamattaṃ, yathā mārena pariyuṭṭhitacitto ajjhotthaṭacitto aññopi koci puthujjano paṭivijjhituṃ na sakkuṇeyya, evameva nāsakkhi paṭivijjhitunti attho. Māro hi yassa keci vipallāsā appahīnā, tassa cittaṃ pariyuṭṭhāti. Yassa pana sabbena sabbaṃ dvādasa vipallāsā appahīnā, tassa vattabbameva natthi, therassa ca cattāro vipallāsā appahīnā, tenassa cittaṃ pariyuṭṭhāsi. So pana cittapariyuṭṭhānaṃ karonto kiṃ karotīti? Bheravaṃ rūpārammaṇaṃ vā dasseti, saddārammaṇaṃ vā sāveti, tato sattā taṃ disvā [M 0.0296] vā sutvā vā satiṃ vissajjetvā vivaṭamukhā honti. Tesaṃ mukhena hatthaṃ pavesetvā hadayaṃ maddati, tato visaññino hutvā tiṭṭhanti. Therassa panesa mukhena hatthaṃ pavesetuṃ kiṃ sakkhissati, bheravārammaṇaṃ pana dasseti. Taṃ disvā thero nimittobhāsaṃ na paṭivijjhi. Jānantoyeva bhagavā kimatthaṃ yāvatatiyaṃ āmantesi? Parato “tiṭṭhatu, bhante bhagavā”ti yācite “tuyhevetaṃ dukkaṭaṃ, tuyhevetaṃ aparaddha”nti dosāropanena sokatanukaraṇatthaṃ. Passati hi bhagavā “ayaṃ mayi ativiya siniddhahadayo, so parato bhūmicālakāraṇañca āyusaṅkhārossajjanañca sutvā mama ciraṭṭhānaṃ yācissati, athāhaṃ ‘kissa tvaṃ puretaraṃ na yācasī’ti tasseva sīse dosaṃ pātessāmi, sattā ca attano aparādhena na tathā vihaññanti, tenassa soko tanuko bhavissatī”ti.

In the phrase 'As one whose mind is obsessed by Māra,' the word 'ti' is merely a particle. The meaning is: 'Just as any other ordinary person whose mind is obsessed and overwhelmed by Māra would be unable to comprehend, so too was he unable to comprehend.' For Māra obsesses the mind of anyone in whom any distortions have not been abandoned. As for one in whom all twelve distortions are entirely unabandoned, nothing more needs to be said. In the elder’s case, four distortions remained unabandoned, which is why his mind was obsessed. But what does Māra do when he obsesses the mind? He shows a terrifying visual object or makes one hear a frightening sound. Then, on seeing or hearing it, beings lose mindfulness and stand with their mouths agape. He inserts his hand through their mouths and crushes their hearts, and then they stand there unconscious. But how could he insert his hand into the elder’s mouth? Instead, he showed him a terrifying object. Seeing it, the elder did not comprehend the hint and suggestion. Though he knew, why did the Blessed One address him up to a third time? It was for the purpose of lessening his sorrow by placing the fault on him, so that when Ānanda later pleaded, 'Let the Blessed One remain, venerable sir!' the Blessed One could say, 'This was your misdeed, Ānanda, this was your fault.' For the Blessed One saw: 'This one has a very affectionate heart toward me. Later, when he hears the reason for the earthquake and about the relinquishing of the life-formation, he will ask me to remain for a long time. Then I will place the fault on his own head, saying, “Why did you not ask me earlier?” Beings are not so tormented by their own transgression, and thus his sorrow will be lessened.'

Gaccha tvaṃ, ānandāti yasmā divāvihāratthāya idhāgato, tasmā, ānanda, gaccha tvaṃ yathārucitaṃ ṭhānaṃ divāvihārāya. Tenevāha – “yassa dāni kālaṃ maññasī”ti.

'Go, Ānanda': Since you have come here for the day's abiding, therefore, Ānanda, go to a place of your liking for the day's abiding. That is why he said: 'For which you now deem it the proper time.'

Māro [V 0.0266] pāpimāti ettha satte anatthe niyojento māretīti māro. Pāpimāti tasseva vevacanaṃ. So hi pāpadhammena samannāgatattā ‘pāpimā’ti vuccati. Bhāsitā kho panesāti ayañhi bhagavati bodhimaṇḍe satta sattāhe atikkamitvā ajapālanigrodhe [P 0.0326] viharante attano dhītāsu āgantvā icchāvighātaṃ patvā gatāsu ayaṃ “attheso upāyo”ti cintento āgantvā “bhagavā yadatthaṃ tumhehi pāramiyo pūritā, so vo attho anuppatto, paṭividdhaṃ sabbaññutaññāṇaṃ, kiṃ te lokavicaraṇenā”ti vatvā yathā ajja evameva “parinibbātu dāni, bhante bhagavā”ti yāci. Bhagavā cassa “na tāvāha”ntiādīni vatvā paṭikkhipi. Taṃ sandhāya idāni “bhāsitā kho panesā”tiādimāha.

Herein, 'Māra, the Evil One': he is 'Māra' because he makes beings engage in what is harmful and thus kills them. 'Evil One' (Pāpimā) is a synonym for him. He is called 'Evil One' because he is endowed with evil states. 'But this was spoken by me': When the Blessed One, after the passing of the seven weeks at the Bodhi tree, was dwelling at the Ajapāla Banyan Tree, after Māra's daughters had come and gone, having met with the frustration of their desire, Māra himself, thinking, 'This is the way,' approached and said: 'Blessed One, the goal for which you fulfilled the perfections has been attained by you; the knowledge of omniscience has been penetrated. What is the use of your wandering in the world?' Then, just as today, he requested: 'Let the Blessed One now attain final Nibbāna, venerable sir; let the Fortunate One attain final Nibbāna.' And the Blessed One rejected him, saying, 'Not yet shall I…' and so on. It is with reference to this that he now said, 'But this was spoken by me…' and so on.

Tattha viyattāti ariyamaggādhigamavasena byattā. Vinītāti tatheva kilesavinayanena vinītā. Visāradāti sārajjakarānaṃ diṭṭhivicikicchādīnaṃ pahānena visāradabhāvaṃ pattā. Bahussutāti tepiṭakavasena bahu sutametesanti bahussutā. Tameva dhammaṃ dhārentīti dhammadharā. Atha vā bahussutāti pariyattibahussutā ceva paṭivedhabahussutā ca. Dhammadharāti pariyattidhammānaṃ ceva paṭivedhadhammānañca dhāraṇato dhammadharāti evampettha attho veditabbo[M 0.0297]. Dhammānudhammappaṭipannāti ariyadhammassa anudhammabhūtaṃ vipassanādhammaṃ paṭipannā. Sāmīcippaṭipannāti ñāṇadassanavisuddhiyā anucchavikaṃ visuddhiparamparāpaṭipadaṃ paṭipannā. Anudhammacārinoti sallekhikaṃ tassā paṭipadāya anurūpaṃ appicchatādidhammaṃ caraṇasīlā. Sakaṃ ācariyakanti attano ācariyavādaṃ. Ācikkhissantīti ādito kathessanti, attanā uggahitaniyāmena pare uggaṇhāpessantīti attho. Desessantīti vācessanti, pāḷiṃ sammā vācessantīti attho. Paññapessantīti pajānāpessanti, pakāsessantīti attho. Paṭṭhapessantīti pakārena ṭhapessanti. Vivarissantīti vivaṭaṃ karissanti. Vibhajissantīti vibhattaṃ karissanti. Uttānīkarissantīti anuttānaṃ gambhīraṃ uttānaṃ pākaṭaṃ karissanti. Sahadhammenāti sahetukena sakāraṇena vacanena. Sappāṭihāriyanti yāvaniyyānikaṃ katvā. Dhammaṃ desessantīti navavidhalokuttaradhammaṃ pabodhessanti, pakāsessantīti attho.

Herein, 'competent' (viyattā) means competent by way of attaining the noble path. 'Disciplined' (vinītā) means disciplined in the same way by the taming of the defilements. 'Confident' (visāradā) means they have attained a state of confidence through the abandoning of things that cause timidity, such as wrong views and doubt. 'Learned' (bahussutā) means they have heard much, in the sense of the Tipiṭaka. 'Preservers of the Dhamma' (dhammadharā) means they bear that same Dhamma. Alternatively, 'learned' means learned in the scriptures and in the penetration. 'Preservers of the Dhamma' means they preserve the Dhamma by upholding both the Dhamma of the scriptures and the Dhamma of penetration; this is how the meaning should be understood here. 'Practicing in accordance with the Dhamma' (dhammānudhammappaṭipannā) means they are practicing the Dhamma of insight, which conforms to the noble Dhamma. 'Practicing the proper way' (sāmīcippaṭipannā) means they are practicing the path that is the sequence of purifications, which is suitable for the purification of knowledge and vision. 'Living in accordance with the Dhamma' (anudhammacārino) means they are accustomed to practicing the states suitable to that path, such as fewness of wishes, which is the practice of effacement. 'Their own teacher's doctrine' (sakaṃ ācariyakaṃ). 'They will declare' (ācikkhissanti): they will speak from the beginning; that is, they will make others learn according to the method they have themselves learned. 'They will teach' (desessanti): they will recite; that is, they will recite the Pāli correctly. 'They will make it known' (paññapessanti): they will make it understood; that is, they will make it manifest. 'They will establish' (paṭṭhapessanti): they will establish it systematically. 'They will open it up' (vivarissanti): they will make it open. 'They will analyze' (vibhajissanti): they will make it analyzed. 'They will make it plain' (uttānīkarissanti): they will make what is not plain and is profound, plain and manifest. 'With the Dhamma' (sahadhammena): with words that have a ground and a reason. 'Convincingly' (sappāṭihāriyaṃ): having made it lead to deliverance. 'They will teach the Dhamma' (dhammaṃ desessanti): they will awaken others to the ninefold supramundane Dhamma; that is, they will make it manifest.

Ettha ca “paññapessantī”tiādīhi chahi padehi cha atthapadāni dassitāni, ādito pana dvīhi padehi cha byañjanapadānīti. Ettāvatā tepiṭakaṃ buddhavacanaṃ saṃvaṇṇanānayena saṅgahetvā dassitaṃ hoti. Vuttañhetaṃ nettiyaṃ “dvādasapadāni [P 0.0327] suttaṃ, taṃ sabbaṃ byañjanañca attho cā”ti (netti. saṅgahavāra).

Here, with the six terms beginning with 'they will make it known,' the six terms of meaning are shown; and with the first two terms, the six terms of phrasing are indicated. By this much, the Tipiṭaka, the word of the Buddha, is shown summarized by the method of exegesis. For this is stated in the Nettipakaraṇa: 'The twelve terms of the sutta are the whole, both the phrasing and the meaning' (Netti. Saṅgahavāra).

Brahmacariyanti [V 0.0267] sikkhattayasaṅgahitaṃ sakalaṃ sāsanabrahmacariyaṃ. Iddhanti samiddhaṃ jhānuppādavasena. Phītanti vuddhippattaṃ sabbaphāliphullaṃ abhiññāsampattivasena. Vitthārikanti vitthataṃ tasmiṃ tasmiṃ disābhāge patiṭṭhahanavasena. Bāhujaññanti bahūhi ñātaṃ paṭividdhaṃ bahujanābhisamayavasena. Puthubhūtanti sabbākāravasena puthulabhāvappattaṃ. Kathaṃ? Yāva devamanussehi suppakāsitanti yattakā viññujātikā devā manussā ca atthi, tehi sabbehi suṭṭhu pakāsitanti attho.

'The holy life' (brahmacariya) refers to the entire holy life of the dispensation, which is comprised in the threefold training. 'Prosperous' (iddha) means prosperous by way of the arising of the jhānas. 'Expanded' (phīta) means it has grown and is fully blossomed by way of the attainment of the direct knowledges. 'Widespread' (vitthārika) means it has become extensive by way of being established in various regions. 'Widely known' (bāhujañña) means known and penetrated by many, by way of the comprehension of the multitude. 'Become extensive' (puthubhūta) means it has attained an extensive state in all respects. How so? 'Until it is well proclaimed among devas and humans' means that it has been well proclaimed by all intelligent beings that exist, both devas and humans.

Appossukkoti nirussukko līnavīriyo. “Tvañhi, pāpima, sattasattāhātikkamanato paṭṭhāya ‘parinibbātu dāni, bhante bhagavā, parinibbātu sugato’ti viravanto āhiṇḍittha, ajja dāni paṭṭhāya vigatussāho hohi, mā mayhaṃ parinibbānatthāya vāyāmaṃ karohī”ti vadati. Sato sampajāno āyusaṅkhāraṃ ossajīti satiṃ sūpaṭṭhitaṃ katvā ñāṇena paricchinditvā [M 0.0298] āyusaṅkhāraṃ vissaji pajahi. Tattha na bhagavā hatthena leḍḍuṃ viya āyusaṅkhāraṃ ossaji, temāsamattameva pana samāpattiṃ samāpajjitvā tato paraṃ na samāpajjissāmīti cittaṃ uppādesi. Taṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ – “ossajī”ti, “vossajjī”tipi pāṭho.

'Untroubled' (appossukko) means without eagerness, with subsided energy. He is saying: 'For you, Evil One, ever since the passing of the seven weeks, have been wandering about crying, “Let the Blessed One now attain final Nibbāna, venerable sir! Let the Fortunate One attain final Nibbāna!” From today onward, be without striving; do not make an effort for my final Nibbāna.' 'Mindful and clearly comprehending, he relinquished the life-formation' means that, having made mindfulness well established and having determined with knowledge, he released and abandoned the life-formation. Here, the Blessed One did not relinquish the life-formation as one might toss away a clod of earth with one's hand. Rather, having entered an attainment for just three months, he produced the thought, 'Hereafter I will not enter it.' It is with reference to this that it is said, 'he relinquished' (ossaji). There is also the reading vossajjī.

Kasmā pana bhagavā kappaṃ vā kappāvasesaṃ vā ṭhātuṃ samattho tattakaṃ kālaṃ aṭṭhatvā parinibbāyituṃ mārassa yācanāya āyusaṅkhāraṃ ossaji? Na bhagavā mārassa yācanāya āyusaṅkhāraṃ ossaji, nāpi therassa āyācanāya na ossajissati, temāsato pana paraṃ buddhaveneyyānaṃ abhāvato āyusaṅkhāraṃ ossaji[P 0.0328]. Ṭhānañhi nāma buddhānaṃ bhagavantānaṃ yāvadeva veneyyavinayanatthaṃ, te asati vineyyajane kena nāma kāraṇena ṭhassanti. Yadi ca mārassa yācanāya parinibbāyeyya, puretaraṃyeva parinibbāyeyya. Bodhimaṇḍepi hi mārena yācitaṃ, nimittobhāsakaraṇampi therassa sokatanukaraṇatthanti vuttovāyamattho. Apica buddhabaladīpanatthaṃ nimittobhāsakaraṇaṃ. Evaṃ mahānubhāvā buddhā bhagavantoyeva tiṭṭhantāpi attano ruciyāva tiṭṭhanti, parinibbāyantāpi attano ruciyāva parinibbāyantīti.

But why did the Blessed One, though able to remain for an aeon or the remainder of an aeon, relinquish the life-formation at Māra's request in order to attain final Nibbāna without remaining for that long? The Blessed One did not relinquish the life-formation at Māra's request, nor would he have failed to relinquish it at the elder's request. Rather, he relinquished the life-formation because after three months there would be an absence of those to be trained by a Buddha. For the Blessed Buddhas remain only for the purpose of training those who can be trained. When there are no more people to be trained, for what reason would they remain? And if he were to attain final Nibbāna at Māra's request, he would have done so earlier, for Māra had requested it at the Bodhi Tree. And the making of the hint and suggestion was for the purpose of lessening the elder's sorrow—this meaning has already been stated. Moreover, the making of the hint and suggestion was for the purpose of demonstrating the Buddha's power. For the Blessed Buddhas, being of such great power, remain by their own inclination and attain final Nibbāna by their own inclination.

Mahābhūmicāloti mahanto pathavīkampo. Tadā kira dasasahassilokadhātu akampittha. Bhiṃsanakoti bhayajanako. Devadundubhiyo ca phaliṃsūti devabheriyo nadiṃsu, devo sukkhagajjitaṃ gajji, akālavijjulatā nicchariṃsu, khaṇikavassaṃ vassīti vuttaṃ hoti.

'A great earthquake': a great tremor of the earth. At that time, it is said, the ten-thousand-world-system shook. 'Frightening': fear-arousing. 'And the celestial drums burst forth': the celestial kettledrums sounded, a deva thundered with a dry thunderclap, unseasonal lightning flashed, and a momentary rain fell—this is what is meant.

Etamatthaṃ viditvāti etaṃ saṅkhāravisaṅkhārānaṃ visesasaṅkhātaṃ atthaṃ sabbākārato viditvā. Imaṃ [V 0.0268] udānanti anavasesasaṅkhāre vissajjetvā attano visaṅkhāragamanadīpakaṃ udānaṃ udānesi. Kasmā udānesi? Koci nāma vadeyya “mārena pacchato pacchato anubandhitvā ‘parinibbātu, bhante’ti upadduto bhayena bhagavā āyusaṅkhāraṃ ossajī”ti. “Tassokāso mā hotu, bhītassa udānaṃ nāma natthī”ti etassa dīpanatthaṃ pītivegavissaṭṭhaṃ udānaṃ udānesīti aṭṭhakathāsu vuttaṃ. Tato temāsamatteneva ca pana buddhakiccassa nipphajjanato evaṃ dīgharattaṃ mayā parihaṭoyaṃ dukkhabhāro na cirasseva nikkhipiyatīti passato parinibbānaguṇapaccavekkhaṇe tassa uḷāraṃ [M 0.0299] pītisomanassaṃ uppajji, tena pītivegena udānesīti yuttaṃ viya. Ekantena hi visaṅkhāraninno nibbānajjhāsayo satthā mahākaruṇāya balakkārena viya sattahitatthaṃ loke suciraṃ ṭhito. Tathā hi devasikaṃ catuvīsatikoṭisatasahassasaṅkhā samāpattiyo vaḷañjeti, sodāni mahākaruṇādhikārassa nipphannattā nibbānābhimukho anappakaṃ pītisomanassaṃ paṭisaṃvedesi. Teneva hi [P 0.0329] bhagavato kilesaparinibbānadivase viya khandhaparinibbānadivasepi sarīrābhā visesato vippasannā parisuddhā pabhassarā ahosīti.

Having understood this meaning—that is, having understood in all respects this meaning designated as the distinction between formations and the cessation of formations—he uttered this inspired utterance after relinquishing all formations without remainder, an utterance that illuminates his own path to the cessation of formations. Why did he utter it? Lest anyone should say, 'The Blessed One, pursued from behind by Māra and afflicted by fear, relinquished the life-formation when urged, “Venerable sir, may the Blessed One attain final Nibbāna,”' it is said in the commentaries that he uttered this inspired utterance, impelled by a surge of joy, to demonstrate this: 'Let there be no opportunity for that, for one who is afraid utters no inspired utterance.' Moreover, since the Buddha's work would be accomplished in just three months, and seeing that 'this burden of suffering carried by me for so long will soon be laid down,' an exalted joy and gladness arose in him as he reflected on the qualities of final Nibbāna. It seems fitting that he uttered this inspired utterance, moved by that surge of joy. For the Teacher, entirely inclined toward the cessation of formations and disposed toward Nibbāna, remained in the world for a very long time for the welfare of beings as if by the force of his great compassion. Thus, daily he enjoyed meditative attainments numbering twenty-four hundred thousand koṭis. Now, since the task of his great compassion was accomplished, being headed for Nibbāna, he experienced no little joy and gladness. For that very reason, just as on the day of the final Nibbāna of the defilements, so too on the day of the final Nibbāna of the aggregates, the radiance of the Blessed One’s body became especially clear, pure, and luminous.

Gāthāya soṇasiṅgālādīnampi paccakkhabhāvato tulitaṃ paricchinnanti tulaṃ, kāmāvacarakammaṃ. Na tulaṃ atulaṃ, tulaṃ vā sadisamassa aññaṃ lokiyakammaṃ natthīti atulaṃ, mahaggatakammaṃ. Kāmāvacaraṃ rūpāvacaraṃ vā tulaṃ, arūpāvacaraṃ atulaṃ. Appavipākaṃ vā tulaṃ, bahuvipākaṃ atulaṃ. Sambhavanti sambhavassa hetubhūtaṃ, upapattijanakanti attho. Bhavasaṅkhāranti punabbhavasaṅkhāraṇakaṃ. Avassajīti vissajjesi. Munīti buddhamuni. Ajjhattaratoti niyakajjhattarato. Samāhitoti upacārappanāsamādhivasena samāhito. Abhindi kavacamivāti kavacaṃ viya abhindi. Attasambhavanti attani sañjātaṃ kilesaṃ. Idaṃ vuttaṃ hoti “savipākaṭṭhena sambhavaṃ, bhavābhavābhisaṅkharaṇaṭṭhena bhavasaṅkhāranti ca laddhanāmaṃ tulātulasaṅkhātaṃ lokiyakammañca ossaji, saṅgāmasīse mahāyodho kavacaṃ viya attasambhavaṃ kilesañca ajjhattarato samāhito hutvā abhindī”ti.

Measurable means weighed, determined; this is kamma of the sensual sphere. Immeasurable means not measurable; or, because no other worldly kamma is similar to it, it is immeasurable, which refers to sublime kamma. Kamma of the sensual sphere or the form sphere is measurable; kamma of the formless sphere is immeasurable. Or, kamma with a small result is measurable; kamma with a great result is immeasurable. Productive of being means a cause for being, that is, it generates rebirth. Formation of being means that which forms renewed existence. He relinquished means he released. The sage means the Buddha-sage. Inwardly delighted means delighted in one’s own inner self. Composed means composed by way of access and absorption concentration. He shattered as if armor means he shattered it like armor. Arisen from oneself refers to the defilement arisen in oneself. This is what is said: He relinquished worldly kamma, known as measurable and immeasurable—which is called 'productive of being' because it has a result, and 'formation of being' because it forms renewed existence—and like a great warrior on the battlefield, being inwardly delighted and composed, he shattered the defilement arisen from himself as if it were armor.

Atha vā tulanti tulento tīrento. Atulañca sambhavanti nibbānañceva bhavañca. Bhavasaṅkhāranti bhavagāmikaṃ kammaṃ. Avassaji munīti “pañcakkhandhā aniccā, pañcannaṃ khandhānaṃ nirodho nibbānaṃ nicca”ntiādinā nayena tulento buddhamuni bhave ādīnavaṃ, nibbāne ca ānisaṃsaṃ disvā taṃ khandhānaṃ mūlabhūtaṃ bhavasaṅkhārakammaṃ “kammakkhayāya saṃvattatī”ti (ma. ni. 2.81; a. ni. 4.233) evaṃ vuttena kammakkhayakarena ariyamaggena avassaji[V 0.0269]. Kathaṃ ajjhattarato samāhito, abhindi kavacamivattasambhavaṃ. So hi vipassanāvasena ajjhattarato, samathavasena samāhitoti evaṃ [P 0.0330] pubbabhāgato paṭṭhāya samathavipassanābalena kavacaṃ [M 0.0300] viya attabhāvaṃ pariyonandhitvā ṭhitaṃ, attani sambhavattā “attasambhava”nti laddhanāmaṃ sabbaṃ kilesajālaṃ abhindi, kilesābhāveneva kammaṃ appaṭisandhikattā avassaṭṭhaṃ nāma hotīti evaṃ kilesappahānena kammaṃ pajahi. Iti bodhimūleyeva avassaṭṭhabhavasaṅkhāro bhagavā vekhamissakena viya jarasakaṭaṃ samāpattivekhamissakena attabhāvaṃ yāpentopi “ito temāsato uddhaṃ samāpattivekhamassa na dassāmī”ti cittuppādanena āyusaṅkhāraṃ ossajīti.

Alternatively, ‘weighing’ means judging, determining. ‘Immeasurable and productive of being’ means both Nibbāna and existence. ‘Formation of being’ is kamma leading to existence. The sage relinquished: the Buddha-sage, weighing by the method beginning, ‘The five aggregates are impermanent; the cessation of the five aggregates, Nibbāna, is permanent,’ saw the danger in existence and the benefit in Nibbāna. He relinquished that kamma which is a formation of being and the root of the aggregates by means of the noble path that destroys kamma, as stated: ‘It leads to the destruction of kamma’ (MN 43; AN 4:233). As for the words, 'inwardly delighted and composed, he shattered as if armor that which arose from himself': He was inwardly delighted by way of insight, and composed by way of serenity. Thus, from the preliminary stage onwards, by the power of serenity and insight, he shattered the entire net of defilements—which is called ‘arisen from oneself’ because it arises in oneself and stands enveloping the individual existence like armor. With the absence of defilements, kamma is unable to link to a new birth and is thus called ‘relinquished.’ In this way, by abandoning the defilements, he forsook kamma. Thus, the Blessed One had already relinquished the formations of being at the foot of the Bodhi tree. Although he was maintaining his individual existence by means of the support of meditative attainments, like a decrepit cart held together with props, he relinquished the life-formation with the thought, ‘Three months from now, I will not give it the support of meditative attainment.’

Paṭhamasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the First Sutta is finished.

2. Sattajaṭilasuttavaṇṇanā

2. Commentary on the Sutta on the Seven Ascetics with Matted Hair

52. Dutiye bahidvārakoṭṭhaketi pāsādadvārakoṭṭhakassa bahi, na vihāradvārakoṭṭhakassa. So kira pāsādo lohapāsādo viya samantā catudvārakoṭṭhakaparivuto pākāraparikkhitto. Tesu pācīnadvārakoṭṭhakassa bahi pāsādacchāyāyaṃ pācīnalokadhātuṃ olokento paññattavarabuddhāsane nisinno hoti. Jaṭilāti jaṭāvanto tāpasavesadhārino. Nigaṇṭhāti setapaṭanigaṇṭharūpadhārino. Ekasāṭakāti ekasāṭakanigaṇṭhā viya ekaṃ pilotikakhaṇḍaṃ hatthe bandhitvā tenāpi sarīrassa purimabhāgaṃ paṭicchādetvā [P 0.0331] vicaraṇakā. Parūḷhakacchanakhalomāti parūḷhakacchalomā parūḷhanakhā parūḷhaavasesalomā ca, kacchādīsu dīghalomā dīghanakhā cāti attho. Khārivividhamādāyāti vividhaṃ khārādinānappakāraṃ pabbajitaparikkhārabhaṇḍikaṃ gahetvā. Avidūre atikkamantīti vihārassa avidūramaggena nagaraṃ pavisanti.

52. In the second sutta, 'outside the gatehouse' means outside the gatehouse of the palace, not of the monastery gatehouse. It is said that this palace, like the Lohapāsāda, was surrounded on all sides by four gatehouses and enclosed by a wall. Among these, outside the eastern gatehouse, he was seated on the excellent Buddha-seat that had been prepared in the shade of the palace, gazing upon the eastern world-sphere. 'Matted-hair ascetics' means those with matted hair, who have adopted the guise of ascetics. 'Nigaṇṭhas' means those who have adopted the appearance of Nigaṇṭhas with white cloths. 'Single-robed ones' means those who, like the single-robed Nigaṇṭhas, wander about having tied a piece of rag around their hand and, with that, covered the front part of their body. 'With overgrown armpit-hair, nails, and body hair' means having overgrown armpit-hair, overgrown nails, and other overgrown body hair; that is, long hair on the armpits and elsewhere, and long nails. 'Carrying various things on a shoulder-pole' means having taken various kinds of renunciant's requisites, such as alkali and other diverse items. 'Passing by not far away' means they were entering the city by a path not far from the monastery.

Rājāhaṃ, bhante, pasenadi kosaloti ahaṃ, bhante, rājā pasenadi kosalo, mayhaṃ nāmaṃ tumhe jānāthāti. Kasmā pana rājā loke aggapuggalassa santike nisinno evarūpānaṃ nagganissirīkānaṃ añjaliṃ paggaṇhātīti? Saṅgaṇhanatthāya. Evañhissa ahosi “sacāhaṃ ettakampi etesaṃ na karissāmi, mayaṃ puttadāraṃ pahāya etassatthāya dubbhojanadukkhaseyyādīni anubhoma, ayaṃ amhākaṃ nipaccakāramattampi na karoti[M 0.0301]. Tasmiñhi kate amhe ‘ocarakā’ti jano aggahetvā ‘pabbajitā’icceva sañjānissati, kiṃ imassa bhūtatthakathanenāti [V 0.0270] attanā diṭṭhaṃ sutaṃ paṭicchādetvā na katheyyuṃ, evaṃ kate pana anigūhitvā kathessantī”ti. Apica satthu ajjhāsayajānanatthampi evamakāsīti. Rājā kira bhagavantaṃ upasaṅkamantopi katipayakālaṃ sammāsambodhiṃ na saddahi. Tenassa evaṃ ahosi “yadi bhagavā sabbaṃ jānāti, mayā imesaṃ nipaccakāraṃ katvā ‘ime arahanto’ti vutte nānujāneyya, atha maṃ anuvattanto anujāneyya, kuto tassa sabbaññutā”ti. Evaṃ so satthu ajjhāsayajānanatthaṃ tathā akāsi. Bhagavā pana “ujukameva ‘na ime samaṇā ocarakā’ti vutte yadipi rājā saddahati, mahājano pana tamatthaṃ ajānanto na saddaheyya, samaṇo gotamo ‘rājā attano kathaṃ suṇātī’ti yaṃ kiñci mukhāruḷhaṃ kathetī’ti vadeyya, tadassa dīgharattaṃ ahitāya dukkhāya saṃvatteyya, añño ca guḷhakammaṃ vivaṭaṃ kataṃ bhaveyya, sayameva rājā tesaṃ ocarakabhāvaṃ kathessatī”ti ñatvā “dujjānaṃ kho eta”ntiādimāha.

'Venerable sir, I am King Pasenadi of Kosala' means: 'Venerable sir, I am King Pasenadi of Kosala; you should know my name.' But why does the king, while seated in the presence of the foremost person in the world, raise his hands in reverential salutation to such naked, inglorious ones? For the purpose of winning them over. This thought occurred to him: 'If I do not do even this much for them, they will think: “We have left behind our children and wives and for his sake endure hardships such as poor food and uncomfortable beds, yet this one does not show us even a small gesture of respect.” Then, thinking, “What is the use of telling this one the truth?” they would conceal what they have seen and heard and not speak. But if I do this, they will speak without concealing anything.' Moreover, he did this also to understand the Teacher’s intention. It is said that for some time, even when the king was approaching the Blessed One, he did not have faith in his perfect self-enlightenment. He thought: 'If the Blessed One knows everything, then when I make this gesture of respect and say, “These are arahants,” he should not approve. But if he goes along with me and approves, whence his omniscience?' Thus he acted in that way to discern the Teacher’s intention. The Blessed One, however, knew this and thought: 'If I say directly, “These are not ascetics but spies,” even if the king believes it, the general public, not knowing the matter, might not believe it. They might say, “The ascetic Gotama says whatever comes to his mouth because the king listens to his words,” and this would lead to their long-term harm and suffering. Also, a secret deed would be revealed. The king himself will declare that they are spies.' Knowing this, he said: 'This is hard to know,' and so on.

Tattha kāmabhogināti iminā pana rāgābhibhavaṃ, ubhayenāpi vikkhittacittataṃ dasseti. Puttasambādhasayananti puttehi sambādhasayanaṃ[P 0.0332]. Ettha ca puttasīsena dārapariggahaṃ, puttadāresu uppilāvitena tesaṃ gharāvāsādihetu sokābhibhavena cittassa saṃkiliṭṭhataṃ dasseti. Kāsikacandananti saṇhacandanaṃ, kāsikavatthañca candanañcāti vā attho. Mālāgandhavilepananti vaṇṇagandhatthāya mālā, sugandhabhāvatthāya gandhaṃ, chavirāgakaraṇatthāya vilepanaṃ dhārentena. Jātarūparajatanti suvaṇṇañceva avasiṭṭhadhanañca. Sādiyantenāti paṭiggaṇhantena. Sabbenapi kāmesu abhigiddhabhāvameva pakāseti.

Therein, by 'one who enjoys sensual pleasures' it shows being overcome by lust; by both it shows a distracted mind. 'A couch crowded with children' means a couch made crowded by children. And here, by the heading 'children,' it indicates the taking of a wife; and by being infatuated with children and wife, it shows the defilement of the mind through being overcome by sorrow on account of their household life and so on. 'Kāsika sandalwood' means fine sandalwood, or the meaning is Kāsī cloth and sandalwood. 'Garlands, perfumes, and ointments' means by one wearing garlands for their appearance and scent, perfume for a pleasant fragrance, and ointment to color the skin. 'Gold and silver' means gold and the remaining wealth. 'Consenting to' means by one accepting. All this reveals only a state of being intensely greedy for sensual pleasures.

Saṃvāsenāti sahavāsena. Sīlaṃ veditabbanti “ayaṃ pesalo vā dussīlo vā”ti saṃvasantena ekasmiṃ ṭhāne saha vasantena jānitabbo. Tañca kho dīghena addhunā na ittaranti tañca sīlaṃ dīghena kālena veditabbaṃ, na ittarena. Katipayadivase hi saññatākāro saṃvutindriyākāro ca hutvā sakkā dassetuṃ. Manasi karotā no amanasi karotāti tampi “sīlamassa pariggaṇhissāmī”ti manasi karontena [M 0.0302] paccavekkhantena sakkā jānituṃ, na itarena. Paññavatāti tampi sappaññeneva paṇḍitena. Bālo hi manasi karontopi jānituṃ na sakkoti. Saṃvohārenāti kathanena.

'By living together' means through cohabitation. 'Virtue is to be known' means it is to be known by one living together, dwelling together in one place, whether 'this one is virtuous or unvirtuous.' 'And that, after a long time, not a short one' means that virtue is to be known over a long time, not a short one. For in just a few days, it is possible to show an appearance of being restrained and of having guarded sense faculties. 'By one who pays attention, not by one who does not pay attention' means that it can be known by one who pays attention and reflects, thinking, 'I will investigate his virtue,' but not by another. 'By one with wisdom' means by one who is wise, a sage. For a fool, even if he pays attention, is not able to know. 'By conversation' means through speaking.

“Yo hi koci manussesu, vohāraṃ upajīvati;

Evaṃ vāseṭṭha jānāhi, vāṇijo so na brāhmaṇo”ti. (su. ni. 619) –

"Whoever among humans lives by a trade, know thus, Vāseṭṭha, he is a trader, not a brahmin."

Ettha [V 0.0271] hi vāṇijjaṃ vohāro nāma. “Cattāro ariyavohārā”ti (dī. ni. 3.313) ettha cetanā. “Saṅkhā samaññā paññatti vohāro”ti (dha. sa. 1313-1315) ettha paññatti. “Vohāramattena so vohareyyā”ti (saṃ. ni. 1.25) ettha kathā vohāro. Idhāpi so eva adhippeto. Ekaccassa hi sammukhākathā parammukhākathāya na sameti, parammukhākathā sammukhākathāya, tathā purimakathā pacchimakathāya, pacchimakathā ca purimakathāya. So kathentoyeva sakkā jānituṃ “asuci eso puggalo”ti. Sucisīlassa pana purimaṃ [P 0.0333] pacchimena, pacchimañca purimena, sammukhā kathitañca parammukhā kathitena, parammukhā kathitañca sammukhā kathitena sameti, tasmā kathentena sakkā sucibhāvo jānitunti pakāsento āha – “saṃvohārena soceyyaṃ veditabba”nti.

Here, in the verse just quoted, trade is called `vohāra`. In 'the four noble expressions' (DN 3.313), `vohāra` is intention. In 'designation, convention, concept, term (`vohāra`)' (Dhs 1313-1315), `vohāra` is concept. In 'he might speak merely by way of convention (`vohāra`)' (SN 1.25), `vohāra` is speech. Here too, that same meaning is intended. For with some people, speech face-to-face does not agree with speech behind the back, nor does speech behind the back agree with speech face-to-face. Likewise, earlier speech does not agree with later speech, nor does later speech agree with earlier speech. Just by their speaking, it is possible to know, 'This person is impure.' But for one of pure virtue, the earlier agrees with the later, and the later with the earlier; speech face-to-face agrees with speech behind the back, and speech behind the back agrees with speech face-to-face. Therefore, showing that purity can be known by how one speaks, he said: 'Purity is to be known by conversation.'

Thāmoti ñāṇathāmo. Yassa hi ñāṇathāmo natthi, so uppannesu upaddavesu gahetabbagahaṇaṃ kattabbakaraṇaṃ apassanto advārikaṃ gharaṃ paviṭṭho viya carati. Tenāha – “āpadāsu kho, mahārāja, thāmo veditabbo”ti. Sākacchāyāti sahakathāya. Duppaññassa hi kathā udake geṇḍu viya uplavati, paññavato kathentassa paṭibhānaṃ anantaṃ hoti. Udakavipphandaneneva hi maccho khuddako mahanto vāti paññāyati.

'Strength' means the strength of wisdom. For one who lacks the strength of wisdom, when calamities arise, not seeing what should be grasped and what should be done, wanders about like one who has entered a house without a door. Therefore, he said: 'In adversity, great king, strength is to be known.' 'By discussion' means through conversation together. For the speech of one with little wisdom floats like a ball on the water, but for one with wisdom who is speaking, his readiness of wit is endless. For it is by the splashing in the water that a fish is recognized as small or large.

Iti bhagavā rañño ujukameva te “ime nāmā”ti avatvā arahantānaṃ anarahantānañca jānanūpāyaṃ pakāsesi. Rājā taṃ sutvā bhagavato sabbaññutāya desanāvilāsena ca abhippasanno “acchariyaṃ, bhante”tiādinā attano pasādaṃ pakāsetvā idāni te yāthāvato bhagavato ārocento “ete, bhante, mama purisā carā”tiādimāha. Tattha carāti apabbajitā eva pabbajitarūpena raṭṭhapiṇḍaṃ [M 0.0303] bhuñjantā paṭicchannakammantattā. Ocarakāti heṭṭhā carakā. Carā hi pabbatamatthakena carantāpi heṭṭhā carakāva nihīnakammattā. Atha vā ocarakāti carapurisā. Ocaritvāti avacaritvā vīmaṃsitvā, tasmiṃ tasmiṃ dese taṃ taṃ pavattiṃ ñatvāti attho. Osārissāmīti paṭipajjissāmi, karissāmīti attho. Rajojallanti rajañca malañca. Pavāhetvāti suṭṭhu vikkhālanavasena apanetvā. Kappitakesamassūti alaṅkārasatthe vuttavidhinā kappakehi chinnakesamassū. Kāmaguṇehīti kāmakoṭṭhāsehi, kāmabandhanehi vā samappitāti suṭṭhu appitā allīnā. Samaṅgibhūtāti sahabhūtā[P 0.0334]. Paricāressantīti indriyāni samantato cāressanti kīḷāpessanti vā.

Thus the Blessed One, without saying directly to the king, 'These are such-and-such,' declared the method for knowing who were arahants and who were not. Having heard this, the king, deeply pleased by the Blessed One's omniscience and the grace of his teaching, expressed his confidence by saying, 'Wonderful, venerable sir!' and so on. Then, reporting those matters truthfully to the Blessed One, he said: 'Venerable sir, these are my men, spies,' and so on. Therein, 'spies' means those who are not renunciants but who, in the guise of renunciants, eat the alms of the country because their work is concealed. 'Spies' means those who move about below. For spies, even when moving about on a mountain top, are still 'those who move about below' because of their base work. Or, 'spies' means spy-men. 'Having spied' means having investigated and examined, that is, having come to know the events in this or that country. 'I will restore them' means 'I will undertake,' that is, 'I will do.' 'Dust and grime' means dust and dirt. 'Having washed off' means having removed by way of a thorough washing. 'With hair and beard trimmed' means with hair and beard cut by barbers according to the method stated in the treatises on adornment. 'With the strands of sensual pleasure' means with the portions of sensual pleasure, or with the bonds of sensual pleasure, they are well provided and attached. 'Endowed' means furnished with. 'They will enjoy themselves' means they will cause their senses to roam all around, or they will cause them to play.

Etamatthaṃ viditvāti etaṃ tesaṃ rājapurisānaṃ attano udarassa kāraṇā pabbajitavesena lokavañcanasaṅkhātaṃ [V 0.0272] atthaṃ viditvā. Imaṃ udānanti imaṃ parādhīnatāparavañcanatāpaṭikkhepavibhāvanaṃ udānaṃ udānesi.

'Having understood this matter' means: having understood this matter concerning those royal men who, for the sake of their own bellies, deceived the world in the guise of renunciants. 'He uttered this inspired utterance' means: he uttered this inspired utterance that makes plain the rejection of dependence on others and of deceiving others.

Tattha na vāyameyya sabbatthāti dūteyyaocarakakammādike sabbasmiṃ pāpadhamme ime rājapurisā viya pabbajito na vāyameyya, vāyāmaṃ ussāhaṃ na kareyya, sabbattha yattha katthaci vāyāmaṃ akatvā appamattakepi puññasmiṃyeva vāyameyyāti adhippāyo. Nāññassa puriso siyāti pabbajitarūpena aññassa puggalassa sevakapuriso na siyā. Kasmā? Evarūpassapi ocarakādipāpakammassa kattabbattā. Nāññaṃ nissāya jīveyyāti aññaṃ paraṃ issarādiṃ nissāya “tappaṭibaddhaṃ me sukhadukkha”nti evaṃcitto hutvā na jīvikaṃ pavatteyya, attadīpo attasaraṇo anaññasaraṇo eva bhaveyya. Atha vā anatthāvahato “ocaraṇa”nti laddhanāmakattā aññaṃ akusalakammaṃ nissāya na jīveyya. Dhammena na vaṇiṃ careti dhanādiatthāya dhammaṃ na katheyya. Yo hi dhanādihetu paresaṃ dhammaṃ deseti, so dhammena vāṇijjaṃ karoti nāma, evaṃ dhammena taṃ na careyya. Atha vā dhanādīnaṃ atthāya kosalarañño puriso viya ocarakādikammaṃ karonto parehi anāsaṅkanīyatāya pabbajjāliṅgasamādānādīni anutiṭṭhanto dhammena vāṇijjaṃ karoti nāma. Yopi idha parisuddhaṃ brahmacariyaṃ carantopi aññataraṃ devanikāyaṃ paṇidhāya brahmacariyaṃ carati, sopi [M 0.0304] dhammena vāṇijjaṃ karoti nāma, evaṃ dhammena vāṇijjaṃ na care, na kareyyāti attho.

Therein, 'one should not strive in every way' means that, like those royal servants who engage in errands and spying, a renunciant should not strive or make an effort in any evil state. The intention is that, without striving anywhere whatsoever, one should strive only in even the slightest meritorious act. 'He should not be another's man' means that a renunciant, in the guise of one gone forth, should not be another person’s servant. Why? Because such a person would have to engage in evil deeds like spying. 'He should not live dependent on another' means one should not sustain one's livelihood by depending on another, such as a powerful person, thinking, 'My pleasure and pain are bound up with them.' Instead, one should be an island for oneself, a refuge for oneself, with no other refuge. Alternatively, since the term 'spying' gets its name from bringing what is not beneficial, one should not live by depending on any other unwholesome action. 'He should not trade with the Dhamma' means one should not teach the Dhamma for the sake of wealth and the like. For whoever teaches the Dhamma to others for the sake of wealth and the like is said to be trading with the Dhamma; one should not engage in such trading. Alternatively, one who, for the sake of wealth and the like, engages in deeds such as spying like a man of the Kosalan king, while adopting the marks of one gone forth so as not to be suspected by others, is said to be trading with the Dhamma. Even one who, while living the perfectly pure holy life here, lives the holy life with an aspiration for some celestial host is also said to be trading with the Dhamma. Thus, 'one should not trade with the Dhamma' means one should not do so.

Dutiyasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the Second Sutta is concluded.

3. Paccavekkhaṇasuttavaṇṇanā

3. Commentary on the Sutta on Reviewing

53. Tatiye [P 0.0335] attano aneke pāpake akusale dhamme pahīneti lobhadosamohaviparītamanasikāraahirikānottappakodhūpanāhamakkhapalāsaissāmacchariyamāyā- sāṭheyyathambhasārambhamānātimānamadapamādataṇhāavijjātividhākusalamūladuccaritasaṃkilesavisama- saññāvitakkapapañcacatubbidhavipallāsaāsavaoghayogaganthāgatigamanataṇhupādānapañcavidha- cetokhilapañcacetovinibandhanīvaraṇābhinandanachavivāda- mūlataṇhākāyasattānusayaaṭṭhamicchattanava- taṇhāmūlakadasākusalakammapathadvāsaṭṭhidiṭṭhigataaṭṭhasatataṇhāvicaritādippabhede attano santāne anādikālapavatte [V 0.0273] diyaḍḍhasahassakilese taṃsahagate cāpi aneke pāpake lāmake akosallasambhūtaṭṭhena akusale dhamme anavasesaṃ saha vāsanāya bodhimūleyeva pahīne ariyamaggena samucchinne paccavekkhamāno “ayampi me kileso pahīno, ayampi me kileso pahīno”ti anupadapaccavekkhaṇāya paccavekkhamāno bhagavā nisinno hoti.

53. Thirdly, the Blessed One was seated reviewing how he had abandoned his own numerous evil, unwholesome states. These are: greed, hatred, and delusion; perverted attention; shamelessness and fearlessness of wrongdoing; anger and hostility; contempt and domineering; envy and stinginess; deceit and fraud; obstinacy and presumption; conceit and arrogance; intoxication and heedlessness; craving and ignorance; the three unwholesome roots; misconduct; defilements; uneven perceptions, thoughts, and proliferation; the four distortions; the taints, floods, yokes, and ties; wrong courses; craving and clinging; the five mental barrennesses, the five mental bondages, the hindrances, and delighting; the six roots of dispute; the body of craving; the seven underlying tendencies; the eight wrongnesses; the nine things rooted in craving; the ten unwholesome courses of action; the sixty-two wrong views; the one hundred and eight kinds of craving-conduct; and other such kinds among the one and a half thousand defilements that had been active in his continuity of existence from beginningless time, along with their concomitants. He was reviewing how these evil, inferior states born of unskillfulness had been abandoned without remainder, together with their latent dispositions, at the very root of the Bodhi tree, cut off by the noble path, reflecting step-by-step: 'This defilement of mine has been abandoned, this defilement of mine has been abandoned.'

Aneke ca kusale dhammeti sīlasamādhipaññāvimuttivimuttiñāṇadassanaṃ cattāro satipaṭṭhānā, cattāro sammappadhānā, cattāro iddhipādā, cattāro ariyamaggā, cattāri phalāni, catasso paṭisambhidā, catuyoniparicchedakañāṇaṃ, cattāro ariyavaṃsā, cattāri vesārajjañāṇāni, pañca padhāniyaṅgāni, pañcaṅgiko sammāsamādhi, pañcañāṇiko sammāsamādhi, pañcindriyāni, pañca balāni, pañca nissāraṇīyā dhātuyo,
